article.name: dsh-layered-memory
article.summary: dsh-layered-memory is a DeepSeek Harness plugin that captures conversations, distills atomic memories, and consolidates them into scene and persona summaries. It stores append-only JSONL sources beside a SQLite search index, optionally uses embeddings, and injects bounded recall before model steps. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark assessment.

who_what.text: The official repository is a public, non-fork GitHub project. Its README describes dsh-layered-memory as a layered memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness with web, TUI and headless integrations; it is a host plugin rather than a hosted memory service.
Catalog ordinal 200 identifies dsh-layered-memory and lists the explicit JunNanLYS/dsh-layered-memory locator. The pinned Atlas entry is retained for roster attribution only.
The official GitHub API identifies main as default branch and resolves it to 69028fbee43e9950fffecc578430909fc827527e; the official main feed reports the same head.

architecture.text: The design separates L0 conversation messages, L1 atomic memories, L2 scene documents and L3 persona summaries. L0 keeps session/message IDs, role, content and timestamps. L1 records carry content, type, family, scene, timestamps, version and source-message IDs.

L0 and L1 have append-only daily JSONL records and a SQLite retrieval index. The README describes FTS and optional vector search; L2 scenes are family-specific Markdown files, while scene navigation and persona summaries feed a stable prompt section.

Host capture and pre-step hooks connect to LLM extraction and deduplication, per-family stores, recall tools, settings UI and optional embedding providers. SQLite is the main search index; JSONL retains the source records.

behavior.text: Capture appends non-off session messages to L0 JSONL and indexes them in SQLite. L1 extraction groups facts into scenes and attaches source message IDs; a separate LLM deduplication decision can store, update, merge or skip a proposal against same-family candidates.

New L1 entries append to JSONL and are indexed in SQLite. An update or merge creates a new record ID and increments the version from replaced targets, then removes prior targets from SQLite; older JSONL entries remain. L2 scene writes are family-specific, and a [DELETED] scene result unlinks its file.

The README documents editing and deleting memories through the settings panel. The inspected model-callable tools expose search and read operations only, not a memory-delete tool; writes flow through capture/distillation and the UI or other host surfaces.

L1 supports FTS5 keyword search, vector search, or hybrid search with reciprocal-rank fusion and a recency-decay weight with a floor. Automatic recall uses the last eight messages, caps its query at 2,000 characters, applies a configured timeout and deduplicates records within a session. A timeout skips injection.

Recall inserts bounded L1 snippets before new user messages. memory_search retrieves L1, conversation_search searches raw L0, and memory_read_scene reads L2/L3 files; persona and scene navigation can also be placed in stable prompt context.

evidence.text: L0 retains source session and message identifiers. L1 carries source_message_ids and version data; append-only JSONL retains earlier records. The README also describes consolidation receipts with an input snapshot, decision details and result hash.
These fields trace records to conversation messages and processing runs. The inspected contracts do not establish independent source-document citations or human verification for each extracted claim.

observability.text: The README describes local logs, activity and recall views, and token-cost accounting grouped by provider, model and distillation layer. The recall hook keeps counts, durations, timeouts and duplicate-suppression totals; cost retention is configurable.

The source bounds recall length and execution time, and embeddings are optional with a local option. Extraction and consolidation still call the configured host/provider LLM; local embeddings alone do not mean those calls stay on-device. No runtime telemetry or cost was collected here.

Scope isolation — unmeasured; family gates and failure-open behavior were inspected, but no cross-family/session workload was run.
Evidence support and citation coverage — unmeasured; source-message lineage was reviewed, but claims were not adjudicated against source material.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured; no timings were collected.
Tokens and cost — unmeasured by this review; accounting is described in project docs, but no provider usage was collected here.
Storage efficiency — unmeasured; no corpus or index size was collected.

limits.text: This inspection covered the pinned English README, core types, L0/L1 stores, L1 extraction, recall hook, model-callable tools, L2 scene store and configuration. It did not inspect every SQLite query, UI route, host integration, provider adapter or deployment path.

Family filters are software routing, not demonstrated authorization: the tool code falls back to unfiltered family search if the host omits the caller agent ID; conversation_search remains global, and a scene read can check the other family. No deployed authorization was evaluated.

Source review cannot establish extraction quality, secure deletion across source logs/backups/rebuilds, runtime stability, real-world isolation, recall quality, latency, cost, storage growth or benchmark performance. Review used official pinned GitHub pages; no local upstream checkout was available.

benchmark.note: No dsh-layered-memory runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. Upstream README benchmark statements were not reproduced or independently adjudicated; source observations and the project fixture are not results.
